The [[Copa Libertadores]] is a seasonal [[association football]] competition that was established in 1960. It begins in mid-January and ends with the final in November of the same year. The Copa Libertadores is open to the league champions of [[CONMEBOL]] member associations; clubs finishing from second to fourth position in the stronger leagues of the region, such as the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian league]], are also included. Originally, only the champions of their respective national league could participate in the competition. However, in 1966 this was changed to allow the runners-up of the leagues to compete.<ref name="RSSSF">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/sacups/copalib.html |title=Copa Libertadores de América |date=3 July 2008 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=13 December 2008 |archive-date=24 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524152408/http://www.rsssf.com/sacups/copalib.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Until 2018, the final was contested over [[Two-legged match|two legs]], one at each participating club's stadium. From 2019, the format was changed, with the final being a single game played at a predetermined venue.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/02/23/copa-libertadores-final-to-be-played-in-single-match-in-2019/110764182/ |title=Copa Libertadores final to be played in single match in 2019 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=23 February 2018 |website=USA Today |access-date=15 June 2020 |archive-date=9 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109034121/https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/02/23/copa-libertadores-final-to-be-played-in-single-match-in-2019/110764182/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

The data below does not include the 1948 [[South American Championship of Champions]], as it is not listed by CONMEBOL either as a Libertadores edition or an official competition. It must be pointed out, however, that at least in the years 1996 and 1997, CONMEBOL entitled equal status to both the Copa Libertadores and the 1948 tournament, in that the 1948 champions ([[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]]) were allowed to participate in the [[Supercopa Libertadores]], a CONMEBOL official competition that allowed participation for former Libertadores champions only (for example, not admitting participation for champions of other CONMEBOL official competitions, such as the [[Copa CONMEBOL]]). The 1948 competition is referred to at the Conmebol website as the competition that, 12 years later, would become the Copa Libertadores.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Vasco Da Gama celebrates 116 years {{!}} CONMEBOL | url=http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/vasco-da-gama-celebrates-116-years | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615191520/http://www.conmebol.com/en/content/vasco-da-gama-celebrates-116-years | archive-date=2018-06-15 | access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref> 

[[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] hold the record for the most victories, with seven wins since the competition's inception. They have also won the competition the most times consecutively, winning four in a row from [[1972 Copa Libertadores|1972]] to [[1975 Copa Libertadores|1975]]. [[Boca Juniors]] are second with six wins; they won their last title in [[2007 Copa Libertadores|2007]]. Peñarol are third with five wins, the most recent being in [[1987 Copa Libertadores|1987]]. Boca Juniors have lost the most finals, having lost on six occasions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/copalibtrivia.html |title=Copa Libertadores Trivia |date=11 September 2004 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=23 July 2009 |archive-date=8 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220808081840/https://rsssf.org/miscellaneous/copalibtrivia.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, 27 clubs have won the competition since its inception in 1960. Clubs from Argentina and Brazil have won 25 Copas Libertadores titles each among them; Uruguayan clubs are third with 8 titles.<ref name="RSSSF" />  Since the inception of the tournament, two finals have been derbies: an Argentine one ([[Superclásico]] in 2018 - the only time, as of 2025, both finalists represented the same country other than Brazil) and a Brazilian one ([[Clássico da Saudade]] in 2020). As of 2025, there have been seven all-Brazilian Copa Libertadores finals, including three back-to-back ones from 2020 to 2022. Brazilian clubs are currently holding a record-breaking winning streak (seven in a row, starting in 2019).{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}}
